context.title: Rivers of Living Water
context.summary: Jesus goes quietly to the Feast of Tabernacles and teaches openly in the temple. Crowds argue over who he is. On the feast's last day he invites the thirsty to come to him, and an attempt to arrest him fails.
context.background: Tabernacles was a joyful autumn harvest festival when families lived in shelters for a week (Leviticus 23). Each morning priests carried water from the pool of Siloam and poured it at the altar, praying for rain. Against that backdrop Jesus cries out about living water.

customs.term: Out of Galilee ariseth no prophet
customs.note: The leaders' claim overlooks Jonah, who came from Gath-hepher in Galilee (2 Kings 14:25).

watchFor: Even Jesus' brothers did not believe in him yet (v. 5).
The officers return saying, 'Never man spake like this man' (v. 46).
Nicodemus speaks up for a fair hearing (vv. 50–51).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Nicodemus
people.summary: The people is victor, a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin. He is first noticed as visiting Jesus by night (John 3:1-21) for the purpose of learning more of his doctrines, which our Lord then unfolded to him, giving prominence to the necessity of being “born again.”

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

events.title: Feast of Tabernacles
events.summary: Passage: John 7:1–52. People: Jesus, Nicodemus. Place: Galilee, Jerusalem. Lasted about 7 days.

events.title: Woman Caught in Adultery
events.summary: Passage: John 7:53–8:11. People: Jesus. Place: Jerusalem.
